regular_hexagon.png.description: A perfect regular pointy-top hexagon with an isotropic mottled texture, face-on.

expected.summary: All residuals ~0 (similarity, affine, homography); central symmetry error ~0; verdict 'strong'. Texture has no preferred direction, so ternary should be mostly 0 (low coherence).

sheared_hexagon.png.description: The regular hexagon after an affine map (anisotropic scale, shear 0.38, rotation 23 deg). Faint horizontal stripes (before warping) show how texture is carried by the transform.

expected.summary: Affine and homography residuals ~0; similarity residual clearly > 0; central symmetry error ~0; verdict 'strong'. After normalisation the stripes should be horizontal again.

perspective_hexagon.png.description: The regular hexagon photographed at an angle (a full perspective homography / keystone). Faint vertical stripes (before warping) converge in the image.

expected.summary: Homography residual ~0; affine residual noticeably > 0 (a parallel-projection model cannot explain convergence); similarity residual largest. With the homography toggle on, the normalised stripes should come out vertical and evenly spaced.

shaded_cube.png.description: Orthographic isometric render of a cube viewed along its body diagonal (near corner at the centre). Three differently shaded faces: top light, right mid, left dark. Each face carries line texture along its long diagonal, i.e. radially out from the centre (top: vertical, right: towards V2, left: towards V4).

expected.summary: All residuals ~0 and central symmetry error ~0. The line texture runs along each convex face's long diagonal (centre to V0, V2, V4), which are the CONCAVE corner's edges. With the default 'edges' ternary convention: CONVEX reading 0, 0, 0 (its edge regions straddle two faces whose stripes differ by 60 deg, coherence ~0.3-0.5, no primary line); CONCAVE reading -1, -1, -1 with a primary line. With the original 'faces' convention it is the mirror image: CONVEX +1, +1, +1 and CONCAVE 0, 0, 0.

cube_off_axis.png.description: Orthographic (parallel) view of a cube from a NON-diagonal direction (rotated 24 deg about x and -28 deg about y). The silhouette is centrally symmetric (opposite sides parallel and equal) but is NOT an affine image of a regular hexagon, and the near corner is off-centre. Faces carry radial (near-corner -> opposite-corner) line texture.

expected.summary: Central symmetry error ~0 (it is a real cube view) but affine residual clearly > 0 and > the regular / sheared samples. This is the case the central-symmetry score exists for: a genuine cube that the affine residual alone would penalise.

irregular_hexagon.png.description: A random irregular hexagon (random angles +/-24 deg and radii 0.55-1.2). Noise control.

expected.summary: All residuals high (comparable to the random-hexagon null baseline), central symmetry error high, verdict 'noise'. If this scores 'strong', the thresholds are too loose.

honeycomb.png.description: A small tiled honeycomb of pointy-top cells (circumradius 70 px, wall-centreline vertices) with pale wax walls, dark honey-filled cells and some capped cells. 'vertices' is the centre cell; 'cells' lists the centre plus three edge-sharing neighbours.

expected.summary: Every cell is a regular hexagon: residuals ~0 for each. Neighbour mode should find exactly one shared edge between the centre and each neighbour. This sample tests edge FINDING, not continuity: once the walls are masked out the cell interiors carry little oriented texture, so continuity scores are mixed and mostly 'unrelated'.

rotated_flat_top.png.description: A regular hexagon turned flat-top (rotated 32 deg: flat-top plus 2 deg so the 'top' vertex is unambiguous). Stripes run parallel to the top edge; a red dot marks the upper-left vertex.

expected.summary: Residuals all ~0 (rotation is part of the similarity). Auto-ordering picks the upper-left vertex (the red dot) as V0, so the normalised image is turned ~28 deg relative to the photo; stepping rotation_offset 0..5 moves the dot round the canonical hexagon and odd offsets swap which interior 'Y' is read as the near corner.
